key_insight: Physically informed basin selection improves discrete origami design by steering optimization toward geometrically compatible, mechanically stiff solutions that survive discretization.
engineering_relevance: A simple initialization bias improves final discrete-design success without additional compute or changes to the optimization procedure.
method: Use automatic differentiation in bilevel optimization to choose among four hinge types at each fold of a fixed-geometry sheet.
Bias initialization toward the stiff, flat hinge option to favor more discretization-robust basins.
Alternatively, penalize frustration and floppiness directly in the outer loss.
evidence_signal: Relaxed optimization succeeds in 97% of runs, but discrete success is 49% at baseline, rising to 69% with the initialization prior and 78% with physical penalties.
watch_item: The abstract evaluates a specific origami design setting; transfer to other discrete mechanical systems remains unestablished.
paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
